topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final course lecture and states its intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Conventional local and cytotoxic cancer therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional therapeutic modalities and their clinical limitations including systemic toxicity and drug efflux resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cellular vulnerabilities and defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss therapeutic approaches that exploit intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities such as hormone dependence, checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic kinase signaling and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the targeting of oncogenic kinase drivers with small-molecule inhibitors and the mechanisms by which cancer cells develop resistance or addiction to these drugs.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates are directed against specific surface antigens on cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and T-cell immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and methods for re-engaging or engineering T-cell responses against cancer.

topics.label: Overall progress, future directions, and systemic challenges in cancer treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on historical treatment outcomes, emerging clinical paradigms, and the ongoing biological and ethical challenges in cancer management.
